finding: Corridor-level abrupt-breakdown episode construction is robust to the temporal clustering threshold.
evidence: 15, 30, and 45 minute clustering all produced 6 corridor episodes.

finding: Most propagation classifications are stable, but some episodes depend on the allowed state-entry lag.
evidence: 4/6 episode classifications were unchanged across 30, 60, and 120 minute propagation windows.

finding: Five minutes before abrupt collapse, event conditions differ only modestly from matched controls and do not show a simple monotonic precursor in every traffic variable.
evidence: Event/control medians: speed 58.10/61.95 mph; flow 419.0/443.5 veh/5min; occupancy 0.1087/0.1150.

finding: Sustained congestion episodes often persist well beyond the initial abrupt onset.
Breakdown probability can be estimated as a stochastic function of current per-lane flow rather than assuming one deterministic capacity threshold.
evidence: 10 observed pre-breakdown flows were combined with 80113 censored free-flow intervals using the product-limit estimator.
